guide.title: How to play
guide.steps.title: Playing a round
guide.steps.setup.title: Choose settings
guide.steps.setup.text: Add 3–20 players by name and choose a game mode and categories. The game draws the words and deals the roles using your choices.
guide.steps.cards.title: Read your private role cards
guide.steps.cards.text: Pass the phone around. Read your own card and hide it before passing the phone on. Your card may show a word, a hint, or just your role.
guide.steps.reveal.title: Play and reveal
guide.steps.reveal.text: Once everyone has read their card, play together at the table. You could take turns giving a short clue and trying to figure out who's bluffing. Select Reveal roles when you're done.
guide.modes.title: Game modes
guide.mode.classic: One imposter gets a hint. Everyone else gets the same secret word. Civilians try to find the imposter, who tries to blend in.
guide.mode.random: Choose a minimum and maximum between zero and the number of players. Use the same value in both fields for a fixed count. Counts outside the special cases below give you a mix of civilians and imposters. Extra roles may narrow the range. The game shows which setup was drawn at the reveal.
guide.mode.none: With zero imposters, everyone is a civilian and gets the same word.
guide.mode.reverse: When there is one fewer imposter than the number of players, only one player gets the word. Everyone else gets the same hint and tries to find the player who has the word.
guide.mode.all: When the number of imposters equals the number of players, everyone gets the same hint. The secret word appears at the reveal.
guide.mode.joker: For five or more players. One imposter gets a hint. The Joker knows the word and tries to get everyone to suspect the Joker.
guide.mode.undercover: Everyone gets a word. One player gets a different, related word. The cards look the same, and both words appear when you reveal the roles.
guide.mode.alliance: For five or more players. Two imposters get the same hint and know who their partner is.
guide.mode.blind: One imposter gets neither the word nor a hint. Everyone else gets the same secret word.
guide.mode.chaos: Choose which modes can be drawn. A higher weight makes a mode more likely. The game shows which mode was drawn when you select Reveal roles.
guide.roles.title: Roles
guide.roles.intro: Players dealt Imposter or Spy count as imposters. Accomplices and Double Agents play on their team.
guide.role.civil: You get the secret word. Give clues that show you know it without saying it outright.
guide.role.imposter: Try to blend in without knowing the secret word. You usually get a hint. In Blind Imposter, your card shows only your role.
guide.role.joker: You know the word and have a goal of your own. Try to make the other players think you're the imposter.
guide.role.spy: Your card shows a different word related to the group's secret word. Try giving a clue that fits in.
guide.role.accomplice: You help the imposters and know one of their identities. You get the same hint as that player. In Blind Imposter, neither of you has a hint.
guide.role.double_agent: You get the secret word and help the imposters. Their identities are secret even to you.
guide.role.undercover: You get a related word that differs from the others'. Your card looks like theirs, and your role is shown at the reveal.
guide.roles.tabletop: Roles for your own house rules
guide.roles.tabletopIntro: Detective and Guardian are roles for groups that deal their own cards and play by house rules. The group decides how to handle their actions at the table.
guide.role.detective: The Detective knows the word and can check whether another player is on the imposter team.
guide.role.guardian: The Guardian knows the word and can protect another player from being called out at the end of the round.
